I have four SteamOS boxes and I use them all the time.

I think that SteamOS has the potential to be a contender in the console market. If you don't think of it as a PC then the things that set it apart from a Window's gaming machine don't seem as big of an issue.

1) It essentially comes pre-modded. You get root on the box. No other consoles do that. Win!

1.1) This means you have the best linux can provide for HTPC as well. XBMC, etc.

2) Your game inventory should continue to work forever*. When the next gen consoles come out .. or the ones after that .. your first gen SteamOS games should "just work". No need to ditch your old library just because you upgraded your gaming hardware. No other consoles do that. Win!

3) There are a ton of free games already available. I count 26 available right now and I know I'm missing some. I could be wrong but I believe that blows the free game ratio out of the water for other consoles.

3.1) Over 1100 games available already and it isn't even "out" yet!

4) No subscription fee for online matchmaking or access to other online features. (XBox live)

5) Standard hardware so if there is a hardware problem you can easily fix it yourself or hire the Geek Squad, etc. (RROD, YLOD, etc)

Now, that doesn't mean it isn't currently without drawbacks.

1) A number of games still have issues either under linux or under SteamOS. The most frustrating of the issues, in my opinion, are the ones relating to controllers. Most games with controller support "just work" with an XBox 360 wired controller for windows (tm) .. but some .. don't. These problems should be completely resolved when the official controller is released by November.

2) Getting multiplayer to work in some Steam (and consequently SteamOS) games is not nearly as easy as it is for most games on other consoles. Some use Steamworks properly and work just fine. Others implement their own systems and work .. the way you'd expect them to work on something other than a console .. with a bit of elbow grease.

3) It is still certainly beta and sometimes things in general don't "just work". I'm optimistic that many will be resolved before November.

4) No exclusive content that I'm aware of. Valve seems to be in favor of putting their awesome games on other consoles, Half-Life, Portal, Left 4 Dead, etc. Others have their Halo, Zelda, Gran Turismo .. while Valve just doesn't seem to play that game.

5) It will probably cost way more than any existing consoles for various reasons.

I'll edit this post if I think of other benefits or drawbacks. :)

My gaming community and I have had over one month of time invested in examining Elite:Dangerous to determine if it would be a suitable game to open a branch (clan, corporation, guild, whatever) in. We were looking for production quality (well thought out game design, UX, so forth), developer responsiveness to relatively large user base requests/gripes, player base size, player base growth, and game traction with active players. Here's what we found:

Foremost, it's pretty. The developer did a fine job with the eye candy. The graphics are appropriate for a space sandbox game while also creatively constructed. There didn't seem to be any exploitable zone/area/map bugs due to poor implementation of zone objects or object scripting. The areas (being procedurally created) are, despite not being individually hand crafted (with the exception of a few areas) are still fun to engage with at first.

Unfortunately, the novelty of this type of construction wears off quickly as there aren't enough intriguing game modes to keep traction with the fickle player base. The player base is relatively small, and of those that do play don't do so on a regular enough basis to be meaningful. Meaningful, as in, person-centric (not NPC) events, actions, and atmosphere (no pun intended) to help keep traction with the players who enjoy this type of game. This is especially true in the case of player driven, game evolving events or actions. PvP is lacking. Although Close Quarters Combat was just recently enabled there doesn't seem to be any effective way of organizing, collaborating, and communicating in-game.

Therefore, the game seems aimless and more of a time sink than something that people can actually engage with on a deeper and more consistent level.

Perhaps you will enjoy the game more once planetary landings are introduced? Elite: Dangerous has always been one of those games that takes place more in your mind than in reality. It's very much an RP kind of game. If you enjoy using your imagination, it can be all things to all men. If you prefer a more tightly scripted environment, with lots of immersive content; it probably isn't for you. I'm not standing up for it's shortcomings at all. It is not perfect as a game by any means. But I like the fact that the devs are building a solid foundation first, and going from there. They have already added a great deal of new content since release, and they show no signs of stopping in the near future.
